rationale: The closest candidates share only routine language of presidential appreciation and requests to convey thanks. C05 most closely parallels the child's acknowledgment followed by a request to express gratitude to others; C09 likewise asks the recipient to convey thanks to assistants; and C03 asks its recipient to convey presidential appreciation to civil-defense workers. None reproduces a distinctive formulation, substantive sequence, or administrative machinery concrete enough to show that it materially supplied the child's drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am deeply appreciative of your telegram concerning the Cuban refugees and of your very generous contribution
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I received the final Report of your Committee with pleasure and appreciation
shared_material.explanation: C05 similarly opens by acknowledging something received and expressing appreciation, but this is conventional correspondence language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: May I ask that you express to them my gratitude for their important part
shared_material.parent_excerpt: ask that you express to the members of the Committee my sincere appreciation for their fine cooperation and effort
shared_material.explanation: C05 has the closest verbal and functional parallel, but asking an addressee to pass thanks to associates is a routine courtesy rather than a material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: May I ask that you express to them my gratitude
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Please convey my thanks also to those who assisted you
shared_material.explanation: C09 uses the same generic request to relay gratitude to third parties.

shared_material.child_excerpt: May I ask that you express to them my gratitude
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hope you will convey to all civil defense workers my personal appreciation
shared_material.explanation: C03 contains another conventional request to convey appreciation, without the child's subject matter or broader drafting structure.
